title: Keep Rust crate and module entrypoints focused
summary: Do not use main.rs, lib.rs, mod.rs or analogous entrypoints as catch-all implementation files.
statement: Keep Rust crate and module entrypoints such as main.rs, lib.rs and mod.rs focused on initialization, orchestration, module declarations and intentional API exposure. Put substantial independent implementation responsibilities in the modules that own them. Cohesive entrypoint-specific logic need not be extracted merely because the entrypoint contains code.
rationale: Owner-approved, public-safe Rust source organization policy. Governs structural cohesion and active maintenance without any source-length threshold.

conditions: An authorized Rust project is being created, implemented, debugged or maintained, and this rule has been explicitly selected for the consumer.
exceptions: Do not change unrelated repositories, bypass higher-priority project restrictions, or treat publication of this rule as automatic activation.
Preserve correctness and established interfaces; sequence risky or conflicting refactors safely and report any block without declaring the debt resolved.
